title: Saṅkalpa for the arghya of atonement (evening)

words.meaning: the giving of the arghya of atonement for the lapse of the time of the evening

samasa.members: सायंसन्ध्या + काल + अतीत + प्रायश्चित + अर्घ्य + प्रदान
samasa.meaning: the giving of the arghya that atones for the lapse of time

translation.literal: I shall perform the giving of the arghya of atonement for the lapse of the time of the evening sandhyā.
translation.readable: I shall offer the arghya that atones for letting the time of the evening Sandhyā pass.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the arghya of atonement in the evening. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.

flags.text: M spells प्रायश्चित्तार्घ्य with one t; the word is prāyaścitta (प्रायश्चित्त), as in M’s own morning and midday forms. A correction of the text should be considered.
